Putting together a team to tackle high-impact space challenges using real data. Looking for curious teammates into web dev, data/ML, UI/UX, or research. If you love building and collaborating, come join us!
summary:
Our project focuses on exploring innovative solutions for the NASA Space Mission Challenge – Mission B. The main objective is to address challenges associated with space missions through technology, creativity, and problem-solving. We aim to propose a solution that can make space exploration more efficient, reliable, and accessible.

The project is designed around identifying a real-world space exploration challenge and developing a technology-based approach to address it. By combining research, innovation, and practical applications, our idea aims to contribute to the future of space exploration.

This challenge is important because advancing space technology helps us understand the universe, overcome complex engineering problems, and create solutions that may also benefit life on Earth. Our goal is to turn an interesting space-related challenge into a meaningful technological concept.
details:
MISSION CONTROL is an interactive educational space mission design game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It allows users to experience the role of a mission designer by planning and managing their own space missions.

Players can select destinations such as the Moon, Mars, Earth orbit and asteroids, choose mission objectives, configure spacecraft and scientific instruments, and select suitable launch vehicles. They must manage important resources such as budget, fuel, power, payload capacity and communication.

The game introduces simulated challenges such as cost increases, power shortages and communication delays. Players must make decisions and adapt their plans to achieve mission objectives. At the end, the system evaluates the mission and provides an outcome based on the decisions made.

The main goal of this project is to make space science and engineering more accessible, interactive and enjoyable for students. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making while helping users understand the challenges involved in real space missions.

The proposed technology stack includes HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React with Vite, along with NASA open educational and planetary reference data. The project combines learning and gaming to create an engaging experience where every decision has a consequence.
